header_summary:
A suite of five interrelated proposals, including [BIP 440](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0440.mediawiki) and [BIP 441](https://github.com/jmoik/bips/blob/gsr-full/bip-0441.mediawiki), aims to restore and expand Bitcoin Script capabilities through the introduction of Tapleaf 0xc2. The framework enables advanced features such as transaction introspection, expressive covenants, extended script primitives, and reusable macros, while maintaining backward compatibility and strict computational limits; details and reference implementations are accessible at the [Bitcoin GSR repository](https://github.com/bitcoin-gsr/bitcoin/tree/gsr).

A new anti-exfiltration protocol, as described by Sjors Provoost and others, addresses the risk of compromised signing devices leaking seed information through manipulated nonces by allowing the host to participate in and verify nonce generation. Despite draft [specifications](https://github.com/AvilaLabs/anti-exfil) and experimental implementations, the protocol lacks formal review, and further peer evaluation is encouraged via available [resources](https://anti-exfil.avilalabs.org).

Decentralized identity solutions leveraging cryptographic keys and anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain, such as the "tulip" protocol, provide pseudonymous, user-controlled identities with secure key rotation and on-chain state management. The scalability of these systems is enhanced by minimizing on-chain interactions and enabling efficient transaction indexing, with technical details outlined in the [tuliproot.com whitepaper](https://tuliproot.com/).

Concerns about privacy in Bitcoin fee payments highlight the risks of transaction linkage when the same wallet is reused; privacy-enhancing strategies under consideration include wallet rotation, CoinJoin, and intermediary services to disrupt payment patterns and improve anonymity.

Advancements in threshold signing for Lightning Network nodes, based on the VPSS1 protocol and informed by prior work such as Iceberg and [shachain-mpc](https://github.com/jespos/shachain-mpc), emphasize full N-of-N participation for secure state updates, robust key management, and careful trade-offs between liveness, security, and storage requirements, particularly for small node groups.

recent_posts.title: [Proposal] Tapleaf 0xc2: An overview of the Great Script Restoration (GSR)
recent_posts.summary: - Five coordinated proposals aim to restore, extend, and modernize Bitcoin Script while preserving compatibility.  - Advanced scripting, transaction introspection, reusable macros, and new primitives enable powerful features and safe execution.  - The framework is a single soft fork, with strict controls, reference implementation, and comprehensive testing available.

recent_posts.title: Draft BIPs: anti-exfil signing for BIP340 and ECDSA, with PSBT fields
recent_posts.summary: - A new anti-exfiltration protocol involves hosts participating in nonce generation to prevent seed leakage.  - Two draft BIPs outline protocol specifications and propose new PSBT fields for enhanced security.  - Current resources include reference implementations and documentation, but formal cryptographic review remains outstanding.

recent_posts.title: TULIP: Permissionless Decentralized Identity
recent_posts.summary: - Decentralized identity uses cryptographic keys and the Bitcoin blockchain to ensure control and verifiability.  - Key rotation and recovery leverage taproot transactions, precommitted chains, and built-in recovery protocols.  - The protocol supports varied applications, efficient indexing, off-chain proofs, and scalable, user-controlled infrastructure.

recent_posts.title: Shielded Bitcoin: Private Transfers on the Bitcoin L1
recent_posts.summary: - Repeated use of the same Bitcoin wallet can link transactions and compromise user privacy.  - Strategies such as using multiple wallets and privacy-enhancing technologies help prevent transaction linkages.  - The current payment system lacks privacy protections, making advanced fee-handling mechanisms necessary.

recent_posts.title: Towards A K-of-N Lightning Network Node
recent_posts.summary: - K − 1 colluding signers can manipulate state in K-of-N schemes, making N-of-N necessary for security.  - The proposed protocol uses VPSS1 for verifiable sharing, requiring all N signers to participate in updates.  - Every update requires unanimous validation, with storage and coordination overhead increasing significantly as group size grows.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary: - The staletip proposal enables Bitcoin nodes to share stale tip block information for enhanced network observability.  - Nodes exchange compressed header sequences and fork points, with communication limited to recent tips for efficiency.  - The initiative addresses block propagation issues, providing tools for faster diagnostics and improved network health insights.

active_posts.title: Lichen: L2s In CHannels ENforced on bitcoin
active_posts.summary: - Users and a central hub co-own contracts, enabling token withdrawal to Bitcoin using multi-signature arrangements.  - Disputed withdrawals are resolved efficiently using RISC Zero, Groth16 proofs, and on-chain BitVMX evaluations.  - The system prioritizes liquidity and security, with tokens always backed by actual reserve assets.

active_posts.title: Quantum Landmines and Vulnerable Coin Auctions
active_posts.summary: - Quantum-safe outputs, landmines, and auctions are proposed to deter quantum theft of legacy coins.  - These mechanisms employ collateral, commit/reveal schemes, and incentive-driven auctions with strategic complexity.  - Designs remain theoretical, emphasizing adaptive, game-theoretic defenses against evolving quantum computing threats.

active_posts.title: Great Consensus Cleanup Revival
active_posts.summary: - The proposal highlights vulnerabilities in Bitcoin, including timewarp and legacy transaction inefficiencies.  - Solutions include adjusting difficulty retargets, limiting legacy scripts, and invalidating certain small transactions.  - Some changes, such as reducing block size, face debate due to potential impacts on scalability and functionality.

active_posts.title: Stats on compact block reconstructions
active_posts.summary: - The efficiency of compact block reconstruction is influenced by node configurations, transaction pools, and mempool activity.  - Enabling mempoolfullrbf significantly improved block reconstruction efficiency, suggesting benefits for network-wide adoption.  - Block reconstruction times varied notably based on transaction request needs and network connectivity conditions.

active_posts.title: Public key recovery for EC leaves in P2MR (BIP-360)
active_posts.summary: - The proposal enables public key recovery from EC signatures, reducing witness size without increasing quantum exposure.  - A recoverable EC leaf allows deriving the public key from the signature, eliminating the need for scripts.  - Security is enhanced by linking the signature challenge to the P2MR root hash and revising nonce derivation.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP30 and BIP34 interaction (was Re: [BIP Proposal] Buried Deployments)
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Duplicate transaction hashes are valid in Bitcoin, and BIP34 does not prevent their occurrence.  - Committed block height helps prevent collisions specifically with coinbase transactions.  - Regular transactions have a low collision risk due to varied inputs and ample entropy usage.

today_in_history_posts.title: LN without SegWit: less efficient or less secure?
today_in_history_posts.summary: - SegWit activation status and its influence on the Lightning Network's feasibility are being questioned.  - There is uncertainty about the security of level 2, compared to the efficiency of level 3.  - Clarification is needed on whether outsourcing channel monitoring could solve level 2's security concerns.

today_in_history_posts.title: Batched Splicing Considered Risky
today_in_history_posts.summary: - Splicing transactions in the Lightning Network introduce vulnerabilities due to lack of effective disincentives for disruption.  - Malicious actors can exploit these vulnerabilities, causing failed transactions and harming involved parties.  - Proposed mitigation strategies increase complexity and trust issues, especially in zero-confirmation channel scenarios.
